newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: IADB chief says Argentine economy on right track.
newsitem.headline: IADB chief says Argentine economy on right track.

text.p: The president of the Inter-American Development Bank said Argentina's economy is on the right track and forecast at least $2.5 billion in IADB funds for the country through next year.
Enrique Iglesias told reporters after meeting with President Carlos Menem that the economy "is on the right track and the trend is positive."
This outlook, he said, "opens the way for the IADB to be active in Argentina, with projects that have a large social element of between $2.5 billion and $3 billion between 1996 and 1997."
It was unclear whether these were new projects.

On Sunday night, International Monetary Fund Managing Director Michel Camdessus praised the Argentine government's plans to make labor laws more flexible and to close a widening fiscal gap through tax increases and reductions in worker benefits.
